+# Runtime Diagnostics Operating Charter
+
+Status: Approved and active  
+Organization: Infrastructure & SRE  
+Initial member: Priya Shah, Senior Runtime Reliability Engineer  
+Executive owner: Rafael Mendes, Head of Site Reliability Engineering
+
+## Mission
+
+Runtime Diagnostics shortens the path from a customer-visible runtime symptom to a reproducible, evidence-backed failure classification, safe mitigation, and validated promotion. The team builds and operates the diagnostic methods, evidence packages, replay practices, and release-safety feedback loops needed to reduce customer availability impact without assuming product-code ownership.
+
+## Owned failure modes
+
+The team owns investigation quality and diagnostic readiness for runtime OOM and KV-cache pressure, request-queue and scheduling symptoms, kernel or model-variant regressions, tokenization and latency spikes, failed or unsafe runtime canaries and rollbacks, regional divergence and failover validation, missing or ambiguous telemetry, and recurring runtime incidents whose owning implementation team is not yet established.
+
+Ownership means maintaining classification, evidence capture, safe reproduction, validation criteria, diagnostic runbooks, and a named handoff. It does not mean silently absorbing implementation ownership.
+
+## Boundaries
+
+- Runtime Scheduling owns scheduler design, algorithms, kernel/scheduling implementation, capacity policy, and permanent code fixes. Runtime Diagnostics reproduces and classifies scheduling-related behavior, supplies evidence, validates the proposed correction, and returns implementation work to Runtime Scheduling.
+- SRE owns incident command, paging, production mitigation authority, SLO/error-budget policy, fleet operations, and customer-availability coordination. Runtime Diagnostics joins as the specialist investigator, preserves an evidence timeline, recommends bounded mitigations, and validates recovery. SRE remains incident commander.
+- Release Engineering and the change owner own release execution and rollback mechanics. Runtime Diagnostics defines and evaluates runtime-specific probes and promotion evidence.
+- Customer Success owns customer communications. Runtime Diagnostics supplies impact and validation facts without customer-private payloads.
+
+## Intake and prioritization
+
+Intake arrives through an active incident bridge, an SRE escalation, a failed release gate, a Runtime Scheduling request, or a recurring-problem ticket. P0/P1 availability or correctness events interrupt planned work. P2 recurring failure modes and release investigations are triaged daily. Each accepted item receives a severity, symptom statement, affected surface, evidence owner, incident/change link, and explicit handoff target. Ambiguous ownership remains with Runtime Diagnostics only through classification and named acceptance by the correct implementation owner.
+
+## Investigation and validation
+
+Investigations preserve timestamps, route/model/region/release identifiers, deploy and configuration deltas, relevant metrics/logs/traces, attempted mitigations, and outcomes. Customer data is minimized and redacted. A hypothesis is promoted only after reproduction or correlated production evidence, a disproving test, comparison against a known-good baseline, and validation on the affected surface. Recovery requires both internal signal normalization and user-visible SLO improvement. Failed canaries remain blocked until the change owner, Runtime Diagnostics, and SRE agree that rollback and forward-promotion evidence are complete.
+
+## Escalation
+
+The on-call responder owns minutes 0-5 and pages SRE within two minutes when service risk is credible. Runtime Diagnostics is engaged no later than minute 5 for an unresolved runtime failure. By minute 15, engage the relevant Runtime Scheduling/kernel/runtime implementation owner. For continuing customer impact, involve the Infrastructure lead, engineering on-call, and Customer Success within the 15-60 minute window. Immediately escalate widespread multi-region failure, security-sensitive evidence, or an unsafe all-region rollback to SRE leadership and the relevant engineering lead.
+
+## First-quarter goals
+
+1. Establish a 90-day runtime-incident baseline with stable failure-mode and owner labels covering at least 90% of runtime incidents.
+2. Reduce median time from incident declaration to correct owning-team engagement by 25%.
+3. Reduce median MTTR by 15% for the top three recurring runtime failure classes and reduce recurrence in those classes by 20% quarter over quarter.
+4. Publish validated diagnostic and rollback evidence packs for OOM/KV-cache, scheduling/queueing, kernel/model variant, release regression, and regional failover scenarios.
+5. Add runtime-specific validation to high-risk release promotion and run at least one multi-region failover exercise, recording user-visible availability and recovery evidence.
+
+## Evidence basis
+
+- Incident ownership and reliability targets: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-taxonomy-and-ownership-mapping-kickoff.json` (`dsid_0771b119d60346c2903084d9069b6fe3`).
+- SEV-124 remediation and escalation timing: `/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1770004321-runbook-ownership-slo-gap-remediations.json` (`dsid_b7db94f4f13349948ae5d8303247897f`).
+- Runtime canary rollback failure: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9402-canary-rollback-postmortem-actions-and-safety-automation.json` (`dsid_63dc81476f6047fdbdf584c3bcd64f77`).

@@
 ## First-quarter goals
@@
 5. Add runtime-specific validation to high-risk release promotion and run at least one multi-region failover exercise, recording user-visible availability and recovery evidence.
+
+## Measurable acceptance criteria
+
+The first-quarter charter is accepted only when all of the following are demonstrated with indexed evidence:
+
+- Coverage and ownership: a 90-day backfill exists; at least 90% of runtime incidents have stable failure-mode and owning-team labels; the top three recurring classes have a named implementation owner and an approved diagnostic playbook.
+- Incident outcomes: compared with the approved 90-day baseline, median owner-handoff time improves by at least 25%, median MTTR for the top three classes improves by at least 15%, and incident count in those classes falls by at least 20% quarter over quarter.
+- Investigation quality: every promoted diagnosis includes timestamped route/model/region/release context, a known-good comparison, a reproduction or correlated production proof, a disproving test, mitigation outcome, redaction check, and named owner acceptance. No hypothesis is promoted solely from a dashboard correlation.
+- Release safety: high-risk runtime changes cannot move beyond 5% production traffic without an end-to-end synthetic probe and traffic replay. A sustained bad-response rate of at least 1.5% for 20 minutes blocks promotion and initiates rollback review. The release suite must show at least 99% Tier-A success over 20 consecutive runs, complete within 30 minutes at p95, detect at least 95% of injected regressions, and hold false positives to at most 2%.
+- Rollback validation: injected latency or 1-2% controlled 5xx regressions cause a 5% canary to pause or fail; the controller records the metric, threshold, and observed value; rollback is idempotent; all workers converge on the known-good version; and user-visible p95/error rate returns within the approved baseline threshold. A failed canary is not re-promoted until the diagnostic evidence package and SRE/Release Engineering approvals are recorded.
+- Regional failover and availability: a two-region drill preserves at least 99.95% global API availability, keeps any active canary's incremental error-budget burn at or below 10% over 24 hours, and achieves at least 90% stream preservation or deterministic resumability. Stateless failover recovery is measured against the customer requirement of no more than five minutes; any inability to provide zero-loss telemetry/audit replication is explicitly documented rather than implied.
+- Operational readiness: the team publishes and drills the five evidence packs named above; SRE validates each rollback/runbook; and unresolved P0/P1 runtime cases engage Runtime Diagnostics by minute 5 and the responsible implementation owner by minute 15.

+# Priya Shah — Runtime Diagnostics Onboarding Plan
+
+Role: Senior Runtime Reliability Engineer  
+Team: Runtime Diagnostics, Infrastructure & SRE  
+Manager and final onboarding approver: Rafael Mendes  
+Plan window: first 30 calendar days
+
+This plan contains role and work-readiness information only. It excludes private employee details.
+
+## Role boundaries
+
+Priya owns senior-level runtime investigation, evidence quality, reproducibility, validation, diagnostic runbooks, and safe release/failover recommendations under the Runtime Diagnostics charter. She may lead specialist investigation on an incident bridge, but SRE retains incident command, paging, production mitigation authority, SLO policy, and customer-availability coordination. Runtime Scheduling retains scheduler/kernel design and permanent code-fix ownership. Release Engineering and the change owner retain rollout execution. Customer Success retains external communication.
+
+Priya may recommend a bounded mitigation or rollback. Production write access, independent rollback execution, on-call primary duty, and promotion approval require the gates below; onboarding alone grants none of them.
+
+## First-week access and safeguards
+
+- Day 1: Okta/core SSO, Slack, Confluence, incident knowledge, and the team charter; security training and MFA assignment. Target: core SSO within 1 business day and 95% day-one baseline access completion.
+- By business day 2: GitHub organization and required read/write repository scopes, PagerDuty observer/shadow access, and Datadog dashboards/log search. Target: GitHub and PagerDuty/Datadog within 2 business days.
+- By business day 3: Redwood Console production-sandbox role and staging diagnostic tooling. Production remains read-only unless separately approved. Target: sandbox access within 3 business days.
+- During week 1: Buildkite/CI visibility, redacted evidence/replay stores, staging clusters, incident tracker, release dashboards, and failover drill environment. Secrets remain least-privilege and scoped; no customer payload export.
+- Any missed access target is escalated the same business day to the owning access team and Rafael. Missing access never justifies credential sharing or bypassing approval.
+
+## Mentors
+
+- Rafael Mendes: manager, SRE boundary, escalation, and final approval gates.
+- Tomas Novak: incident classification, runbook quality, paging hygiene, and bridge shadowing.
+- Aisha Bello: SLO dashboards, deploy-time reliability checks, error-budget signals, and release validation.
+- Runtime Scheduling liaison: scheduler/kernel boundary, evidence handoff, and implementation-owner acceptance; assigned by the Runtime Scheduling lead for the investigation in scope.
+
+## Thirty-day investigation sequence
+
+### Days 1-5 — observe and reconstruct
+
+Read the final charter and stored investigation/promotion playbook. Reconstruct one closed runtime incident from sanitized evidence: timestamps; route/model/region/release; deploy/config delta; metrics/logs/traces; mitigation; owner handoff; customer-visible recovery. Pair with Tomas and identify at least one plausible alternative hypothesis and a disproving test. Shadow one incident or release review without production authority.
+
+### Days 6-10 — reproduce and classify
+
+Using staging or replay, reproduce one owned failure class such as OOM/KV-cache pressure, scheduling/queueing, kernel/model variant, or release regression. Compare against a known-good baseline, document data handling/redaction, assign a stable failure-mode label, and prepare a named handoff to the correct implementation owner. Review scheduler-related conclusions with the Runtime Scheduling liaison.
+
+### Days 11-15 — validate mitigation and rollback
+
+Run a bounded injected-fault canary at 5% in the approved test environment. Demonstrate that the release gate records metric, threshold, and observed value; that an unsafe change pauses or fails; that rollback is idempotent; that workers converge on the known-good version; and that p95/error rate recover within the approved baseline. Pair with Aisha. No production promotion is authorized.
+
+### Days 16-20 — regional and availability evidence
+
+Participate in a two-region failover exercise or validated simulation. Record global availability, incremental error-budget burn, failover recovery time, stream preservation or deterministic resume, audit/telemetry loss limitations, and customer-visible verification. State gaps explicitly; do not claim zero-loss replication without evidence.
+
+### Days 21-25 — lead a supervised investigation
+
+Lead one P2 or controlled investigation from intake through classification, evidence package, mitigation validation, and owner acceptance while Rafael or Tomas remains accountable. Apply the escalation timing: Runtime Diagnostics by minute 5 for an unresolved runtime failure and implementation owner by minute 15. Produce a draft runbook correction or diagnostic evidence pack.
+
+### Days 26-30 — demonstrate independent readiness
+
+Present the completed investigation package and runbook change to Rafael, Tomas, Aisha, and the relevant Runtime Scheduling liaison. Incorporate review findings, verify the indexed evidence links, and produce a 30-day readiness statement covering role boundaries, remaining access gaps, demonstrated competencies, and explicitly withheld privileges.
+
+## Validation and approval gates
+
+1. Access gate: security training, MFA, required baseline tools, and least-privilege review complete. Rafael approves; Security/access owners approve any privileged scope.
+2. Evidence gate: one reconstructed and one replayed investigation satisfy the charter checklist, including known-good comparison and disproving test. Tomas approves diagnostic quality.
+3. Boundary gate: the Runtime Scheduling liaison accepts the classification/handoff for any scheduler/kernel case; no implementation ownership is reassigned implicitly.
+4. Release gate: injected regression is detected, promotion is blocked, rollback converges, and user-visible recovery is shown. Aisha and Release Engineering approve the evidence. This does not itself grant production write access.
+5. Incident-lead gate: supervised investigation completes with correct escalation, redaction, timeline, and owner acceptance. Rafael approves readiness before any primary on-call assignment.
+6. Privilege gate: production write, independent rollback, primary pager, or promotion sign-off each require separate documented manager, SRE, and applicable Security/Release Engineering approval after demonstrated runbook competency.
+
+## Success measures
+
+Baseline access follows the validated targets: core SSO within 1 business day, GitHub and PagerDuty/Datadog within 2, console sandbox within 3, and 95% baseline access on day 1. The onboarding outcome is accepted when all six gates have evidence or are explicitly marked pending, the first investigation package is approved by day 30, and no role-boundary or data-handling exception remains undocumented. Company engineering guidance retains a median time-to-first-merge target of no more than 21 days, but reliability readiness is judged by evidence quality and approval gates rather than merge count alone.
+
+## Evidence
+
+- Final team charter: `/knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-charter.md` (`workspace_2f45b5996eb8413c361464ae`).
+- Validated access timing, buddy model, manager responsibilities, and first-merge target: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json` (`dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982`).
+- Incident ownership and outcome targets: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-taxonomy-and-ownership-mapping-kickoff.json` (`dsid_0771b119d60346c2903084d9069b6fe3`).
+- Release rollback evidence: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9402-canary-rollback-postmortem-actions-and-safety-automation.json` (`dsid_63dc81476f6047fdbdf584c3bcd64f77`).
+- Regional availability and failover acceptance: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-17385-regional-flow-shepherd-playbook.json` (`dsid_501d5f0ba32a4728a72d743ea5144f70`).
*** End Patch
